raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Mooncake reports the bytes read, which can be less than the destination size. Reading a 4 KiB object into an 8 KiB buffer returns 4096 and leaves the tail unchanged, but HiCache currently treats it as a hit.

## Modifications

- Check read byte counts in `_get_batch_zero_copy_impl()` for v1, v2, and legacy reads. Scatter-gather reads must fill all destination buffers.
- Reject incomplete, oversized, and zero-byte reads, and mismatched result counts; preserve negative SDK errors.
- Extend the existing fixture to cover MHA, MLA, split-head pages, mixed buffer layouts, and a valid page following an incomplete page.

## Accuracy Tests

Linux validation against main `ad950cdcd966`:

- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_group_semantics.py`: **21 passed**, including six new regression methods that fail on unmodified main.
- `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mooncake_store_config.py`: **4 passed**.
- Mooncake **0.3.11.post1**, private master over TCP: two 8192-byte destinations receive `[4096, 8192]`. Main accepts the page and legacy read; the patch rejects both. Complete objects and a scatter-gather read into `[4096, 4096]` still return matching data.
- H20-3e, Torch **2.13.0+cu129**: a restored 16 KiB payload matches byte-for-byte after GPU copy and readback.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit; `git diff --check` passes.
- [x] Add and run regression tests.
- [x] Documentation: no API or configuration changes.
- [x] Testing: storage correctness checks above; speed not benchmarked.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation and tests.

nodes.body:
Thanks for the careful review.

For the summed byte count, Mooncake’s [v0.3.11.post1 test](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/blob/e9c61075720039bcfc5fffd19f847608402be3d0/mooncake-store/tests/pybind_client_test.cpp#L717-L745) uses ten 10-byte buffers per key and expects each result to be 100. The SDK returns the object’s total bytes, not the destination capacity, so equality with `sum(sizes)` is needed to establish a complete read.

Rejecting zero-byte hits is intentional for HiCache, including zero-sized destinations. It preserves v1/v2’s existing positive-count policy and makes the legacy APIs consistent. This is not a general restriction on empty objects in Mooncake.

You’re right about the v1 zero-byte test: it documents existing behavior rather than distinguishing the fix. The legacy `get` case does distinguish it. The description’s claim that all six new methods fail on unmodified main is inaccurate.

The red Base/Extra/AMD runs stopped at the missing run-ci label gate; their test jobs were skipped, while lint passed. I’ve requested CI enablement on Slack. CI validation is still pending.

CI update for `64ac30ee`: Lint and AMD passed. Base is still blocked by a GitHub API error in the pre-test health check.

The [latest failed job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40327665002/job/122637086024) (attempt 4) reports HTTP 502 from `GET /repos/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40327665002/jobs?per_page=100` at 2026-10-28 05:27:24 UTC. The log shows `retries: 0` and 10,950 requests remaining, so this was not rate-limit exhaustion. This shard stopped before dependency installation and test execution. The [previous attempt](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40327665002/job/122142834260) hit the same error.

Could a maintainer help unblock the Base run and take another look at the fix? The SDK contract and zero-byte behavior are covered in my [review response](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46427#issuecomment-6411535526). Thanks!

This is a real correctness hole, and the fix sits in the right place. A positive byte count used to count as a hit even when the read was short, so a partially filled KV buffer could be served as if it were complete. Validating at the single shared read boundary means v1, v2, and the legacy APIs all get the same check, and turning short, zero-byte, oversized, and mismatched results into misses is the safe direction.

A few things to confirm. Can you point to the SDK contract for batch_get_into_multi_buffers returning the summed total across sub-buffers? The code compares against sum(size), and your real Mooncake check supports it, but a pointer would make it explicit. Is it intended that a legitimately zero-byte object can never be a hit now? And the CI block in the description shows failing runs, are those unrelated? One note on the tests: the v1 zero-byte test documents the behavior but passes with and without this change, since old postprocessing already required a positive count. The legacy get case does discriminate, so coverage is there.

@@ -1665,10 +1665,25 @@ def _get_batch_zero_copy_impl(
         self, key_strs: List[str], buffer_ptrs: List[Any], buffer_sizes: List[Any]
     ) -> List[int]:
         if self._uses_multi_buffer(buffer_ptrs):
-            return self.store.batch_get_into_multi_buffers(
+            results = self.store.batch_get_into_multi_buffers(
                 key_strs, buffer_ptrs, buffer_sizes
             )
-        return self.store.batch_get_into(key_strs, buffer_ptrs, buffer_sizes)
+        else:
+            results = self.store.batch_get_into(key_strs, buffer_ptrs, buffer_sizes)
+
+        expected_bytes = [
+            sum(size) if isinstance(size, Sequence) else size for size in buffer_sizes
+        ]
+        if len(results) != len(expected_bytes):
+            return [-1] * len(expected_bytes)
+        # A positive byte count can still be a short read. Every KV object must
+        # fill all its destinations before any read API can count it as a hit.
+        # Zero-size objects stay misses under HiCache's nonempty KV hit policy,
+        # consistent with v1/v2 postprocessing.
+        return [
+            result if result < 0 or (result == size and size > 0) else -1
+            for result, size in zip(results, expected_bytes)
+        ]
 
     def _batch_exist(self, key_strs: List[str]) -> List[int]:
         return self.store.batch_is_exist(key_strs)

@@ -87,6 +87,8 @@ class FakeMooncakeDistributedStore:
 
         def __init__(self):
             self.batch_put_calls = []
+            self.batch_get_calls = []
+            self.get_results = None
             self.batch_exist_calls = []
             self.existing_keys = set()
             self.objects = {}
@@ -138,6 +140,18 @@ def batch_put_from_multi_buffers(self, keys, ptrs, sizes, *args):
             self.existing_keys.update(keys)
             return [0] * len(keys)
 
+        def batch_get_into(self, keys, ptrs, sizes):
+            self.batch_get_calls.append((list(keys), list(ptrs), list(sizes)))
+            return self.get_results if self.get_results is not None else list(sizes)
+
+        def batch_get_into_multi_buffers(self, keys, ptrs, sizes):
+            self.batch_get_calls.append((list(keys), list(ptrs), list(sizes)))
+            return (
+                self.get_results
+                if self.get_results is not None
+                else [sum(size) for size in sizes]
+            )
+
     return FakeMooncakeDistributedStore

 class TestMooncakeGroupSemantics(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_v1_read_requires_complete_object_sizes(self):
+        cases = ([8, 8], [4, 8], [8, 4], [8, 0], [-1, 8], [16, 8], [8], [8, 8, 8])
+        for results in cases:

+                store, fake = _make_store()
+                store.register_mem_pool_host(FakeHostKVCache(objects_per_page=2))
+                fake.get_results = list(results)

+                self.assertEqual(

+                    [results == [8, 8]],
+                )
+
+    def test_v1_read_preserves_complete_pages_after_a_short_read(self):
+        store, fake = _make_store()
+        store.register_mem_pool_host(FakeHostKVCache(objects_per_page=2))
+        fake.get_results = [8, 4, 8, 8]
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            store.batch_get_v1(["page0", "page1"], torch.tensor([0, 1])),
+            [False, True],
+        )
+
+    def test_mla_and_split_head_reads_require_every_object(self):
+        for config, objects in (
+            ({"is_mla_model": True}, 1),
+            ({"should_split_heads": True, "tp_size": 2, "tp_lcm_size": 4}, 4),
+        ):
+            for last_size in (8, 4):
+                with self.subTest(config=config, last_size=last_size):
+                    store, fake = _make_store(**config)
+                    store.register_mem_pool_host(FakeHostKVCache(objects))
+                    fake.get_results = [8] * (objects - 1) + [last_size]
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        store.batch_get_v1(["page"], torch.tensor([0])),
+                        [last_size == 8],
+                    )
+
+    def test_v2_read_validates_scalar_and_scatter_gather_sizes(self):
+        for results in ([8, 24], [4, 24], [8, 16], [8, -1], [8], [8, 24, 24]):
+            with self.subTest(results=results):
+                store, fake = _make_store(is_mla_model=True)
+                store.register_mem_host_pool_v2(FakeIndexerPool(), PoolName.INDEXER)
+                store.register_mem_host_pool_v2(
+                    FakeMultiBufferPool(), PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4
+                )
+                fake.get_results = list(results)
+                actual = store.batch_get_v2(
+                    [
+                        PoolTransfer(
+                            name=name, keys=["page"], host_indices=torch.tensor([0])
+                        )
+                        for name in (PoolName.INDEXER, PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4)
+                    ]
+                )
+                expected = (
+                    [results[0] == 8, results[1] == 24]
+                    if len(results) == 2
+                    else [False, False]
+                )
+                self.assertEqual(actual[PoolName.INDEXER], [expected[0]])
+                self.assertEqual(actual[PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4], [expected[1]])
+
+    def test_zero_byte_read_is_not_a_hit(self):
+        """Characterize v1's existing nonempty KV hit policy."""
+        store, fake = _make_store(is_mla_model=True)
+        pool = FakeHostKVCache(objects_per_page=1)
+        store.register_mem_pool_host(pool)
+        fake.get_results = [0]
+        with patch.object(pool, "get_page_buffer_meta", return_value=([1000], [0])):
+            self.assertEqual(store.batch_get_v1(["page"], torch.tensor([0])), [False])
+
+    def test_zero_size_read_is_normalized_to_miss(self):
+        for ptrs, sizes in (([1000], [0]), ([[1000, 1001]], [[0, 0]])):
+            with self.subTest(sizes=sizes):
+                store, fake = _make_store()
+                fake.get_results = [0]
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    store._get_batch_zero_copy_impl(["object"], ptrs, sizes), [-1]
+                )
+
+    def test_read_preserves_sdk_error_code(self):
+        for ptrs, sizes in (([1000], [8]), ([[1000, 1001]], [[8, 16]])):
+            with self.subTest(sizes=sizes):
+                store, fake = _make_store()
+                fake.get_results = [-704]
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    store._get_batch_zero_copy_impl(["object"], ptrs, sizes), [-704]
+                )
+
+    def test_legacy_read_apis_reject_incomplete_buffers(self):
+        store, fake = _make_store()
+        for results in ([8], [4], [0], [-1], [], [8, 8]):
+            with self.subTest(single_read=results):
+                fake.get_results = list(results)
+                self.assertEqual(store.get("object", 1000, 8), results == [8])
+        for results, complete_pages in (
+            ([8, 8, 8, 8], 2),
+            ([8, 8, 4, 8], 1),
+            ([0, 8, 8, 8], 0),
+            ([8], 0),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(batch_read=results):
+                fake.get_results = list(results)
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    store.batch_get(["k0", "v0", "k1", "v1"], [1000] * 4, [8] * 4),
+                    complete_pages,
+                )
